record.paper_title: Open Problems in Heavy Quarkonium Physics
record.context_brief: Chromoelectric correlator and bottomonium ground state
record.original_question: What is the correct chromoelectric correlator governing the dominant non-perturbative correction to heavy-quarkonium masses, and does an accurate determination of that correlator support or invalidate a perturbative treatment of the bottomonium ground state? In the framework discussed in the paper, the non-perturbative mass shift depends on the correlator hE(t)E(0)i(μ); existing quenched lattice estimates give an inverse correlation length of about 1.25 GeV, a scale that is not only larger than the typical binding-energy scale E but also comparable to the momentum-transfer scale p. The open problem is therefore to determine this correlator accurately enough to decide whether the apparent success of perturbative calculations for the ground-state bottomonium system is genuinely justified.

evidence.quote: A precise determination of this formula would need having an accurate determination of the chromoelectric correlator.
This may potentially question the whole perturbative approach to the ground state of bottomonium.
Only a better determination of the chromoelectric correlator can solve the conundrum.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider heavy quarkonium in the framework of (potential) non-relativistic QCD, where the leading non-perturbative correction to the mass of a heavy quark–antiquark bound state is governed by the gauge-invariant chromoelectric two-point correlator

  D_E(t;μ) = ⟨0| T E^a_i(t,0) φ_{ab}(t,0) E^b_i(0,0) |0⟩(μ),

with E^a_i the chromoelectric field, φ_{ab}(t,0) a straight adjoint Wilson line from (0,0) to (t,0), and μ a renormalization scale. Within the multipole expansion, the dominant non-perturbative mass shift δM_NP of a Coulombic heavy quarkonium state is a functional of D_E that depends on its short-distance behaviour and on its integrated low-frequency content; this contribution must be parametrically smaller than the perturbative binding energy E ∼ m α_s^2 (and ideally smaller than effects controlled by the typical momentum p ∼ m α_s) for the perturbative treatment of the state to be self-consistent.

Currently available (quenched) lattice estimates of D_E indicate an inverse correlation length of approximately 1.25 GeV, which is larger than the binding-energy scale E of the bottomonium ground state Υ(1S) and comparable to its typical momentum p.

Problem. Determine the chromoelectric correlator D_E(t;μ) (including its proper renormalization and matching to perturbative QCD) accurately enough to compute the leading non-perturbative mass shift of the Υ(1S) bottomonium ground state, and decide whether its size is small compared with the perturbative contributions—thus justifying a perturbative treatment of the Υ(1S)—or whether it is comparable to or larger than them, invalidating that treatment.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent lattice and perturbative studies (2024–2025) continue to compute chromoelectric field correlators in SU(3) gauge theory using gradient flow and multilevel algorithms, including NLO perturbative analyses in Euclidean space and applications to quarkonium dynamics. These works refine the renormalization and short-distance behaviour of the correlator but do not yet provide a determination precise enough to conclusively settle whether non-perturbative corrections to the Υ(1S) bottomonium ground state are small or large compared with the perturbative contributions; the problem therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: Lattice study of correlators of chromoelectric fields for heavy quarkonium dynamics in the quark-gluon plasma
status_evidence.snippet: Lattice calculation of the correlators of two chromoelectric fields in the adjoint representation connected by adjoint Wilson lines... with discussion of the renormalization of the correlators on the lattice.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent (2025) lattice work to determine the chromoelectric correlator with improved renormalization.

status_evidence.title: Perturbative study of NLO chromoelectric correlators in Euclidean space
status_evidence.snippet: NLO perturbative computation of chromoelectric correlators in Euclidean space.
status_evidence.claim: Ongoing perturbative refinements indicate the precise determination needed for the bottomonium ground-state question is still being pursued.

status_evidence.title: Adjoint chromoelectric and -magnetic correlators with gradient flow
status_evidence.snippet: Gradient flow smearing applied to pure gauge theory chromoelectric correlators to control divergences.
status_evidence.claim: Technique development continues, indicating the correlator is not yet determined to required accuracy.
